subject: allele reversed in common factor model

messages.author: 01406da19ce63546
messages.subject: allele reversed in common factor model
parts:
Dear All,

I used Genomic SEM to estimate a common factor model. I realized that one of the summary statistics had reversed A1/A2 alleles. Would this impact the latent factor I estimated? Do I need to reverse the alleles and rerun the model?

Many Thanks, 
Leah

messages.author: 3b39745f73eec779
messages.subject: Re: allele reversed in common factor model
parts:
Hi Leah,

You might be fine, if the alleles in all steps are flipped and there wasn’t a constraint that interfered with the model finding a solution with a negative loading. But being sure would take quite a bit of work/checking and going forward you’d have to explain the flip to anyone who’d work with the results/files. You’re probably going to be doing future you a favor by fixing this fully by rerunning if it’s feasible (shouldn’t slow you down nothing prevents you from writing things up etc).


Best,
Michel

One further question is that I’d like to use the latent variable created in genomic SEM in gwas-by-subtraction. Would this lead to any problems?

Best, 
Leah

messages.subject: Re: allele reversed in common factor model
parts:
Hi Leah,

If you want to do GWAS by subtraction of a factor, its probably best  to do that in one single step/model.

wrt the first question, lets just say its prob best to rerun with the allele's flipped correctly in the long run, though it could be fine, can't say without more info (outputs/logs etc)

Best,
Michel
